messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High OOM rate detected on gpu-node-72 in us-west-2. 14 OOMs in last 5m, average tail latency spike > 3x. Severity: P1. auto-escalate=true :rotating_light:

sanjay (oncall): I’m on it. pulling logs now. tagging runtime and sre.

emily (sre): ack. grabbing dmesg and allocator traces. initial glance shows repeated cudaErrorMemoryAllocation around the same model family. headroom reported at ~450MB free by monitor but OOMs still happen.

ryan (runtime): hmm that sounds like reserved-blocks or fragmentation. can you paste the allocator dump? ran a quick `nvidia-smi`?

sanjay (oncall): attaching snippets: ```
[ 12:03:20 ] allocate 1.2GiB failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[ 12:03:20 ] headroom reported: 470MB
[ 12:03:20 ] reserve_map: reserved_total=1.5GiB reserved_in_use=1.48GiB sparepool=32MiB
```

emily (sre): thanks. that reserve_in_use ~= reserved_total suggests shadow/reserve saturation. but sparepool small. looks like fragmentation: many ~8-64MiB holes.

ryan (runtime): can we repro with smaller seq length? is this KV cache growth? which model?

sanjay (oncall): model = rdx-13b-q4 (dedicated). seq len distribution: a few requests at 8k tokens, most 1k. KV cache footprint spikes when long context tails come in.

marta (customer-ops): any customer impact? we're seeing increased 5xxs from one enterprise tenant. they reported degraded qps earlier.

emily (sre): yes, routing shows ~30% request failures for that tenant in us-west-2. short-term: recommend throttling long contexts and routing to fallback model version while we mitigate.

ryan (runtime): immediate mitigation steps I can do now: 1) disable prefetch on node-72 to avoid speculative reserve claims 2) increase sparepool to 256MiB 3) enable aggressive slab consolidation to reduce fragmentation (risky)

sanjay (oncall): do step 1 and 2 now. skip 3 until we have telemetry. I'll run the commands.

sanjay (oncall): run: ```
# disable prefetch for node-72
curl -X POST -d '{"node":"gpu-node-72","prefetch":false}' https://infra-api.internal/nodes/config
# bump sparepool
curl -X POST -d '{"node":"gpu-node-72","sparepool_mb":256}' https://infra-api.internal/nodes/config
```

emily (sre): applying now. watching OOM counter. also attached allocator histogram: lots of free buckets in small sizes, but large contiguous blocks are rare.

ryan (runtime): good. also toggle model-level KV cache throttle for rdx-13b-q4 to cap KVs per request to 512 entries until further notice. That will limit memory per long request.

marta (customer-ops): notifying affected tenant: "We're mitigating a memory issue in us-west-2 that may affect requests with very long contexts. We're routing long requests to a fallback model and expect service to stabilize in ~15-30m." Do you want me to push an incident banner?

sanjay (oncall): yes please. banner + support channel.

emily (sre): after disabling prefetch + sparepool bump: OOMs dropped from 14->2 in the last 5m. latency back toward normal for non-long requests. the remaining OOMs are correlated with containers that recently restarted (ghost reserve leak?).

ryan (runtime): container crashloop could leave orphaned reserves at the driver level. check cuda-reserve maps and `nvidia-persistenced` status. can we trigger a graceful drain of the offending containers and restart?

sanjay (oncall): initiating rolling restart of serving-container on gpu-node-72 for pods with age > 10m. using graceful drain script.```
[sanjay (oncall) runs restart script]

sanjay (oncall): restart complete for 6 pods. telemetry shows reserve_map now: reserved_total=1.5GiB reserved_in_use=1.1GiB sparepool=256MiB. OOMs now 0 in last 2m.

emily (sre): nice. looks like a combination: 1) KV cache growth + a few long contexts 2) prefetch speculative claims reduced sparepool 3) container restarts left driver-side reservations in an inconsistent state causing fragmentation.

ryan (runtime): for medium-term: propose these actions: - introduce periodic reserve compaction on idle nodes - surface per-container reserved footprint in the console - make prefetch opt-in on high-memory models - KV cache soft cap with graceful tail-truncation

marta (customer-ops): I updated customers and support. asking legal/enterprise for potential SLA impact for the tenant. they want a postmortem and root cause summary.

sanjay (oncall): marking incident as "mitigated" for now. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then hand off to EM to run full RCA.

emily (sre): capturing logs and allocator dumps into /incidents/3543219876/artifacts. adding timeline and commands run.

ryan (runtime): follow-up action items assigned: - runtime: reserve compaction PR (ryan) - infra: improve sparepool defaults and prefetch guardrails (emily) - product: add per-tenant long-context throttling knobs (marta)

marta (customer-ops): thanks team. I'll schedule a customer update postmortem sync and draft the external summary.

incident-bot: Incident 3543219876 status changed: MITIGATED by sanjay (oncall) at 3543219940.

sanjay (oncall): closing here. will open a separate RCA thread with findings.
